title: Name of PowerToy : Color Picker for English UK

judgment.rationale: The report identifies the locale and exact spelling discrepancy with screenshots. There is no assignee or linked implementation; the previous ownership claim was unsupported.
evidence: PowerToys 0.80.1 displays Color Picker in an English UK environment; the reporter expects Colour Picker and compares Paint.
The only comment is automated similarity matching, not a localization decision or confirmed duplicate.
The live timeline contains no linked fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare en-GB resource fallback on the current build, then approve a targeted localization plan if the discrepancy remains.

fix_assessment.rationale: A locale-specific resource correction is applicable if current en-GB fallback still selects the US spelling. No matching public PR was found by issue-number and en-GB/Color searches.

proposed_fixes.title: Provide the approved en-GB Color Picker display-name translation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the displayed name falls back to the en-US resource because an en-GB translation is absent or not selected. The report does not establish whether the module name is intentionally invariant.
plan: Reproduce with Windows and PowerToys set to English UK and identify the displayed-name resource and its fallback chain.
Check the localization policy for module names, then update the en-GB translation through the existing localization pipeline rather than globally replacing Color.
Verify the Settings navigation, module page and picker UI consistently consume the localized display name without changing module identifiers or paths.
verification: Compare en-GB and en-US side by side; en-GB should use the approved regional spelling while en-US remains Color Picker.
Check another locale and ensure machine-readable module names and persisted settings keys are unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The locale and incorrect text are explicit, but resource selection and naming policy need maintainer verification.

issue_context.summary: A UK English user reports that Color Picker keeps the US spelling in PowerToys 0.80.1, unlike the Colour Picker wording shown in Paint.
known_information: The body includes the actual and expected spelling and two screenshot links.
The issue remains open, unassigned and labeled as both bug and translation.
No human comment establishes a duplicate or an intentional invariant product name.
inferences: A regional-resource fallback or missing translation is plausible; an intentional branding choice remains an alternative.
issue_context.analysis: This is sufficient for a maintainer locale comparison without asking the reporter to repeat screenshots. The stale artifact incorrectly treated an empty assignee as active ownership.
initial_investigation: Read the full report and sole comment and checked the paginated live timeline.

Located src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw and src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw in the current repository tree; resource values and en-GB runtime selection were not tested.
Issue-number and en-GB/Color PR searches returned no matching fix; automated similarity suggestions are not duplicate evidence.

actions.label: Compare Color Picker in en-GB and en-US

reproduce.title: Check regional spelling and resource fallback
reproduce.version_requirement: Current supported PowerToys build; compare reported 0.80.1 only in an isolated historical test if needed.
prerequisites: A Windows test account with English UK available and access to PowerToys language settings.
steps: 1. Select English UK for Windows and PowerToys and restart PowerToys.
2. Open Settings navigation, the Color Picker page and the picker/editor; record the visible module names.
3. Repeat under English US and inspect the resource key and fallback chain for each differing surface.
4. Confirm the established localization policy before changing the name.
reproduce.expected_result: Regional spelling follows the approved localization policy; internal identifiers and other locales do not change.
